front: What does a successful ping from PC-A to PC-B prove?
back: PC-A exchanged ICMP echo messages with PC-B just now. It does not test any application or any other destination.

front: What must be true of the IPv4 addresses of two PCs on the same LAN?
back: Each PC needs a different address. Two devices using the same address create an address conflict.

front: Which IOS modes do the prompts >, # and (config)# identify?
back: User EXEC, privileged EXEC and global configuration.

front: Which command saves the running configuration, and which command shows that it was saved?
back: `copy running-config startup-config` saves it. `show startup-config` displays the saved copy.

front: What is the difference between the running and the startup configuration?
back: Running: in use now, held in RAM, lost at restart. Startup: the saved copy in NVRAM, loaded when the device starts.

front: What does `<cr>` mean in IOS context help?
back: The command is complete as typed: pressing Enter will run it.

front: Why can switch S1 carry frames between PC-A and PC-B without an IP address of its own?
back: A switch forwards Ethernet frames between its ports. An IP address on a switch is needed only to manage the switch itself.

front: Which three things do you save separately in this course?
back: The device's startup configuration, the Packet Tracer .pkt project, and the app's study-progress export.

front: What is the difference between `exit` and `end` in configuration mode?
back: `exit` goes back one level. `end` (or Ctrl+Z) returns straight to privileged EXEC.

front: What do `% Incomplete command` and `% Ambiguous command` mean?
back: Incomplete: the command needs another argument. Ambiguous: your abbreviation matches more than one command, so type more letters.
It merges the saved configuration into the running one. It does not save your work and it is not an undo.
